text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- Under refugee return plan, some 40,000 people could be return to their homes in 1997.

- President's deputy chief-of-staff Vesna Skare-Ozbolt says that there will be no "transitional solution" for Vukovar, that is, no postponing establishment of full Croatian authority in Serb enclave .
- "Croatia-A Nation Forged in War", by journalist Marcus Tanner, is published by Yale University Press.
- The current Yugoslav Army commander, general Momcilo Perisic, is sentenced in absentia to 20 years in prison for artillery attacks on Zadar he ordered in 1991.
- Dubrovnik planning for some two million overnight stays during the 1997 tourist season.
- Ruling Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) captures 42 seats in the parliament's House of Counties, while the opposition wins 21 seats.
- Foreign investment does not equal sell-off of Croatia, Economy Minister Nenad Porges says in an interview.
- There is not even a theoretical possibility of us forging a coalition with the ruling HDZ party, says leader of Croatian Social Liberal Party (HSLS), Vlado Gotovac.
- Government accepts plan for return of refugees and announces the establishment of agency in charge of real estate transactions.
